rules.advisoryReason: NEW 2026-08-18. Spec 35A F.1: a composite's selectors.typography must target its own ROOT, never a child's dead BEM class. Guards the THIRD defect layer (declared / rendered / CONSUMED) that no other rule checks: a native typography control can exist, render, and save a value while its generated CSS never reaches the painted element. WORKED EXAMPLE: sgs/hero's 7 declared native typography controls are silent no-ops because selectors.typography targets .sgs-hero__headline, which edit.js sets only as an InnerBlocks TEMPLATE child's className — the generated scoped rule sits at (0,2,0) and cannot beat that child block's own inline typography at (1,0,0,0), this framework's HC2 rule. A NAIVE TEXT SEARCH CANNOT SEE THIS, proven live: it returned 2 false positives (sgs/modal, sgs/social-icons — the WP-core-generated wp-block-sgs-* root class, legitimately absent from source) and MISSED hero entirely, because .sgs-hero__headline IS present in hero's files, just never as a DOM class attribute. The rule instead resolves the effective selector, extracts the class token, and classifies via AST (InnerBlocks-template ownership) plus a DOM-emission scan excluding this codebase's CSS-selector-building idiom (_sel / 'selector' / wp_style_engine). A REAL ENGINE BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE BUILD, and it matters beyond this rule: comparing AST line numbers against ctx.cache.strippedText() line numbers is WRONG, because strippedText() blanks a multi-line comment's entire character range INCLUDING its newlines, collapsing them and shifting every subsequent line number — that silently produced ZERO findings on hero, the one block this rule exists to catch. Character OFFSETS (node.start/node.end) stay aligned between raw and stripped text; line numbers do not. strippedText() also strips only /* */ in PHP and never //, so the rule carries its own quote-aware // stripper. EXPECTED POPULATION declared before the first live run per _meta.zeroIsAClaim: 25 blocks declare supports.typography, 11 resolve to the WP-root fallback and are skipped, and of the remaining 14, 3 were predicted to flag. MEASURED: exactly 3, the same three — reconciled, no surprises. rules.advisoryReason: NEW 2026-08-18. Guards the defect class NO other gate in the ~52-segment chain can see: not 'is what this block has correct?' but 'is the fix somebody already applied STILL THERE?'. Earned by a live, measured regression: commit 4a859e42 (2026-08-14) fixed the Spec 35 A5 nested-panel double-title by pairing className="sgs-nested-tools-panel" in edit.js with a hide rule in editor.css; two UNRELATED commits then deleted the className again - c5acba10 (a shadow migration) from button/edit.js and f6f3c033 (the colour rollout) from tabs/edit.js - both through a green build. 25% of the fix was gone in 4 days and nothing noticed, because an orphaned CSS rule matching nothing is not a syntax error, not a dead control and not a style violation. EXPECTED POPULATION declared before the first live run per _meta.zeroIsAClaim: 7 blocks reference the marker, 2 FLAG (button, tabs - both CSS-without-JS) and 5 pass (decorative-image, label, option-picker, quote, testimonial). PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL WITHOUT MUTATING THE REPO: the two known-failing sites exist in the tree right now, so the negative control is a READ - no fixture plant, honouring D659 (2026-08-18) where a subagent restored a defective line to test its detector and a deploy shipped it. Comments deliberately do not count: the JS side reads ctx.cache.strippedText() and the CSS side strips block comments here, because a marker inside a commented-out attribute is a DELETED fix a naive text search scores as present - fixture comment-only-marker-with-css is the mustFlag control proving exactly that, alongside css-without-marker and marker-without-css; both-halves-present and neither-half-present prove it stays silent on a healthy pairing and on a block that never had the fix. The rule asserts PAIRING only, never adoption - 'should this block have the fix at all?' is a completeness question this rule deliberately does not answer. Generalises by adding one row to DURABILITY_MARKERS: any hand-applied fix planting a paired token gets a free regression test.
rules.resolution: RESOLVED SAME COMMIT, and the resolution was NOT what the plan assumed. The plan said 'restore the marker'; investigating both findings proved the opposite. The marker was originally planted on a PanelBody/ToolsPanel pair with IDENTICAL titles (button: 'Shadow'/'Shadow'; tabs: 'Colours'/'Colours') - the genuine double-title defect. Both nestings have since been removed legitimately by the very commits that dropped the className: c5acba10 replaced button's nested ToolsPanel with a direct <ShadowControl>, and f6f3c033 replaced tabs' bespoke Colours panel with SgsColourPanel (tabs now has ZERO <ToolsPanel> in the whole file). Restoring the marker on button would have hidden an inner <h2> whose title now DIFFERS from its parent, deleting a meaningful label. So the correct repair was to delete the two orphaned CSS rules (19 lines each, pure deletions), which is what shipped. openBacklog 2 -> 0. Promotion to gate is the next step and deliberately NOT taken in the introducing commit (E6 point 9).

rules.advisoryReason: NEW 2026-09-01. Two sanitisers exist for user-supplied SVG markup and MUST be used everywhere SVG is mounted or echoed: JS side sanitiseSvg() (src/utils/sanitise-svg.js) wrapping any editor dangerouslySetInnerHTML; PHP side wp_kses( markup, sgs_allowed_svg_tags() ) (or the identical underlying sgs_svg_kses_allowed_tags(), or the shared sgs_tier_media_render(), which sanitises SVG tiers internally) wrapping any render.php echo. Flags TWO independent shapes: (1) edit.js dangerouslySetInnerHTML mounting SVG-shaped content without sanitiseSvg( appearing in the same locus; (2) render.php directly reading an SVG-content-shaped attribute without the file showing wp_kses()+allowlist or sgs_tier_media_render() evidence. EXPECTED POPULATION stated before the first live run, by hand-tracing (independent of this rule's own code) every real SVG-mounting/echoing surface tree-wide, 2026-09-01: JS side — `grep -rln dangerouslySetInnerHTML src/blocks/*/edit.js` returns exactly THREE files (hero, media, timeline), all three already wrapping their __html value in sanitiseSvg(...). PHP side — sgs/media echoes via wp_kses()+sgs_allowed_svg_tags() directly; sgs/before-after's render.php never touches beforeSvgContent/afterSvgContent directly at all (delegated to a sibling media-render.php's own wp_kses()+sgs_svg_kses_allowed_tags() call, outside this rule's render.php-only scope by construction); the 7 bgSvgContent-declaring blocks (container/hero/multi-button/physics-canvas/site-footer/site-header/trust-bar) null bgSvgContent out of their own attrs copy and delegate to SGS_Container_Wrapper::render(), again outside this rule's per-block render.php scope; hero's splitSvg IS read directly but is then routed through sgs_tier_media_render(), which sanitises internally. Expected live population: 0 — this is a guard against future regressions (the same shape as rule 38's own 0-population claim), not a live backlog to clear. The attribute-name heuristic (`Svg(Content[A-Za-z0-9]*|Tablet|Mobile)?$`) was itself investigated empirically before finalising: the naive "contains Svg AND Content" heuristic under-matches sgs/hero's splitSvg/splitSvgTablet/splitSvgMobile (raw markup, no "Content" substring at all) — a full census of every Svg-named attribute in the tree (58 rows, 9 blocks) split cleanly into 13 markup-carrying names (matched) and 6 styling/behaviour names per bgSvg-declaring block (bgSvgPosition/Animation/AnimationSpeed/Opacity/MinHeight/TextShadow, correctly excluded) with zero ambiguous cases. Positive/negative controls proven via --self-test: sgs/media and sgs/before-after (the two named acceptance-criterion blocks) both silent, plus a sanitised-both-silent fixture proving the rule does not simply flag every SVG mention, plus a no-svg-block-silent negative control.

NEW 2026-09-04 (Bean-scoped Task 2a, road-to-uniform plan). Checks Spec 35A PART F's 'a reset control that does nothing' anti-pattern: a ToolsPanelItem `hasValue={ () => ... }` whose body references zero identifiers (a constant masquerading as a check, e.g. `() => false`) or `onDeselect={ () => ... }` whose body calls zero functions (e.g. `() => {}`, resets nothing). AST walk over each block's own edit.js, mirroring check-empty-inspector-containers.js's precedent (its own header records two regex attempts that got this exact class of question wrong in opposite directions). Deliberately skips a hasValue/onDeselect prop that is not a literal arrow/function expression (a reference to an externally defined function) — cannot see into it, false absence is safe. EXPECTED POPULATION stated before the first live run, by a method independent of this rule's own code: `grep -rn "onDeselect={ () => {} }\|onDeselect={() => {}}\|hasValue={ () => false }\|hasValue={ () => true }\|hasValue={() => false}\|hasValue={() => true}" src/blocks/*/edit.js` returns 0 hits tree-wide. MEASURED: `node run.js --json` reports 0 FLAGGED for this rule, matching the independent grep exactly — a genuine clean result on the shapes checked, not a claim the anti-pattern can never occur (the self-test fixtures prove the rule CAN flag real code: bad-hasvalue, bad-ondeselect).

NEW 2026-09-04 (Bean-scoped Task 2b, road-to-uniform plan). Checks Spec 35A PART F's 'colour-only state indicator' anti-pattern (WCAG 1.4.1 use-of-colour): a persisted UI state selector (aria-current/aria-selected=true/aria-checked=true/aria-expanded=true/.is-active/.is-selected/.is-current/[open]/a BEM --active|--current|--selected modifier — deliberately never a bare :hover, which is transient) whose UNIONED declared properties (collected across every rule matching the same normalised selector in the file, not just the first occurrence — sgs/accordion's [open] case is the named real example of a paired split) are colour-only (color/background-color/border*-color/outline-color/fill/stroke/text-decoration-color). Property classification: 'warn' when every property is unambiguously colour-only; 'informational' (never a hard fail) when the set also carries an AMBIGUOUS property (background/box-shadow/filter/opacity) that could be a flat colour swap or a real shape/texture change depending on the actual value; not flagged at all when any CLEAR non-colour property exists (font-weight, border-width, transform, text-decoration, etc.). Per-block scope, reads each block's own style.css; CSS parsing primitives (brace-matching parseBlock/parseDeclarations, comment-stripping) are a copied algorithm from scripts/check-shared-css-state-rules.js, not a require() of that file — its own bottom calls main() unconditionally at module scope with no require.main guard, so importing it directly would run its CLI as a side effect. MEASURED live (`node run.js --json`): 22 findings across 12 blocks, including all three real candidates the task brief named to verify against — sgs/post-grid's pagination current-page indicator (line 583, warn), sgs/product-card's active thumbnail (line 843, warn), and sgs/buybox's current value-ladder row (line 277, informational, box-shadow-only).

NEW 2026-09-04 (Bean-scoped Task 2c, road-to-uniform plan). Checks Spec 35A PART F's 'help text not linked via aria-describedby' anti-pattern. PRECONDITION VERIFIED LIVE before building, per the task brief's stop-and-report gate: Playwright against the sandybrown canary block editor (sgs/accordion's native 'Allow multiple open') confirmed WordPress DOES self-wire aria-describedby for its OWN useBaseControlProps-based native controls (TextControl/ToggleControl/SelectControl/etc.) — rendered DOM showed input aria-describedby pointing at the help

's id. Scope therefore narrows to what self-wiring cannot reach: a raw mount wrapping a child that is NOT one of WordPress's self-wiring native controls (a bare Button, ColorPalette, a repeater), with no literal aria-describedby anywhere in that subtree. Whole-tree scope (not per-block) because both confirmed real candidates are SHARED src/components/*.js files, not any one block's own edit.js — a per-block-only rule would be structurally blind to them, the same gap rule 24's own header documents for GradientOverlayControl.js. `help` presence is judged OPTIMISTICALLY (a first draft required a literal string and MISSED both named candidates, because LinkPopoverControl.js/DesignTokenPicker.js pass `help` through as a parameter, `help={ help }`, an Identifier reference, not authored inline) — only a syntactically obvious empty value (empty string literal, literal undefined/null/false) is treated as 'no help'. MEASURED live (`node run.js --json`): 3 findings — src/components/LinkPopoverControl.js:267 and src/components/DesignTokenPicker.js:583 (both explicitly named/verified by the task brief; GradientCapableColourControl.js:414 was hand-read as the correctly-wired reference, confirmed NOT flagged — it manually wires aria-describedby and does not use at all), plus one previously-unknown genuine finding: src/components/DateTimePickerField.js:101.

NEW 2026-09-05. Bean's architecture decision (this session): WordPress's native supports.typography is FULLY REPLACED, everywhere, by the shared TypographyControls component (edit.js) + sgs_typography_css_rule() helper (render.php). Under that decision ANY remaining native supports.typography declaration is a violation on its own, independent of rule 33's separate 'does the selector even work' question (rule 33's own backlog is 0 -- its 3 predicted findings were fixed in the 2026-09-02 uniformity sweep -- while 25 blocks still declare supports.typography; those 25 are THIS rule's population, not rule 33's). Flags three kinds: (A) native-typography-declared -- a real (non-meta) supports.typography sub-flag is true; (B) typography-gap-no-mechanism -- an element manifest entry's attrMap names a REAL typography member (css:font-size/font-weight/line-height/etc, never css:color alone) but the block has neither native typography nor the shared component; (C) typography-component-partial -- exactly one of {TypographyControls in edit.js, sgs_typography_css_rule() in render.php} is present, the 'both' bucket a prior risk-assessment agent flagged. FIRST DRAFT GATED (B)/(C) ON clusters.includes('text') ALONE and produced 19 FALSE-POSITIVE gap findings -- every one resolved to a colour-only element (an icon's currentColor fill, a modal close button, a plain wrapper colour override) that shares the text cluster's css:color member with genuine typography elements but has zero font-* attrMap keys. Corrected same day to require a real typography-specific attrMap key; proven live by disabling the fix and confirming the regression fixture (text-cluster-colour-only-not-typography) was then wrongly flagged. MEASURED live 2026-09-05 (node run.js --json), post-fix: 25 native-typography-declared, 0 typography-gap-no-mechanism, 4 typography-component-partial (sgs/button, sgs/heading, sgs/label, sgs/text -- CLAUDE.md's own 'canonical' TypographyControls adopters, which mount the shared editor control but hand-roll their OWN render-side CSS via object-tiered attrs rather than calling sgs_typography_css_rule(), which still expects the older flat-scalar shape -- a genuine, previously undocumented architecture drift, not a detector defect). The codemod's target population is the 25 native blocks plus these 4 partial-adopters; no total-gap case exists today.
